changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.onFailMessage: config_audit_event entity_type CHECK already admits the #1368 names
preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'ck_config_audit_event_entity_type' AND pg_get_constraintdef(oid) LIKE '%WORKSPACE_LLM_MODEL%'

changeSet.comment:
Admit the entity types #1368 introduces: the per-purpose binding that replaces the named agent config, the two budget caps, and a workspace's own LLM connections and models. DROP + ADD, the same shape 1784242879917-3/-4 use — the ADD validates every existing row in one pass (no rewrite) under a momentary ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, trivial at this table's size.
The value set is a superset of what anything writes, by design: AGENT_CONFIG, AI_CONFIG_BINDING, WORKSPACE_LLM_BUDGET and WORKSPACE_BYO_LLM_BUDGET are names earlier rows were written under and stay admitted forever, because trg_config_audit_event_block_mutation refuses any UPDATE except erasure — rewriting history to tidy the vocabulary is precisely the mutation this table exists to prevent. The set must match ConfigAuditEntityType exactly; ConfigAuditImmutabilityIntegrationTest reads pg_constraint on the migrated schema and fails if the two drift.

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Create the append-only LLM accounting ledger: one row per provider attempt of an LLM-consuming unit of work. (source_type, source_id, source_attempt) is the idempotency key — a retried attempt bills once, and a second attempt of the same job is a distinct, separately billable row. pricing_state is tri-state so an unpriced call surfaces as unverifiable instead of silently counting as $0. cost_usd is NUMERIC(18,6): a NUMERIC(12,6) ceiling of $999,999.999999 would silently clamp — and so undercharge — a genuinely larger monthly figure against a cap set above it. applied_* freezes the rates actually charged, so a past dollar stays falsifiable no matter how the catalog is repriced later; they are soft refs with no FK because the ledger must survive catalog-row deletion.

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: The workspace's monthly cap on its instance-funded LLM spend in USD; null = uncapped.

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.onFailMessage: nothing to backfill from: agent_job.llm_cost_usd has already been dropped by changeSet -43, so this backfill has already run

changeSet.comment:
Backfill the ledger from detection/replay job history. NOT EXISTS keeps a re-run additive-only; the WHERE mirrors the executor's write guard (usage reported OR a cost recorded). Classification is conservative: a positive cost is genuinely PRICED, a zero cost with no tokens burned is a genuine no-op (NO_CHARGE), and anything else stays UNPRICED so it surfaces as unverifiable rather than as a silent $0.
funding_source is INSTANCE for every backfilled row, written explicitly rather than left to the column default so the decision is visible where the rows are made. Historical spend predates the two-purse model entirely, and which purse paid is NOT recoverable from the database: the worker-pod override (HEPHAESTUS_WORKER_LLM_API_KEY) beat the per-workspace key whenever it was set, and it lived in a pod environment variable that was never persisted. INSTANCE is the right side to err on. It is the operator's own instrument — visible in the admin console and raisable by the person who reads this changelog — whereas the WORKSPACE purse is a different party's money, and a workspace admin given a month of pre-upgrade spend they cannot explain has no way to dispute it. It is also the only self-consistent choice at the moment of the upgrade: every carried-over workspace connection arrives disabled (changeSet -33), so there is no own-provider configuration for a WORKSPACE-funded row to belong to. Inventing per-row provenance in an append-only ledger whose purpose is to keep a past dollar falsifiable would be worse than one documented, uniform assumption.
changeSet.sql: -- The guarded cost is computed once, in the inner SELECT, and both stored and classified -- from that one value. Deriving pricing_state from the raw double instead would misclassify -- the values the guard rejects — PostgreSQL orders NaN above every number, so a NaN cost -- reads as "> 0" (PRICED) while the column it lands in is NULL (unverifiable). INSERT INTO llm_usage_event (id, workspace_id, job_type, source_type, source_id, source_attempt, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, total_calls, cost_usd, pricing_state, funding_source, occurred_at) SELECT gen_random_uuid(), src.workspace_id, src.job_type, 'AGENT_JOB', src.id, 0, src.llm_model, src.input_tokens, src.output_tokens, src.cache_read_tokens, src.cache_write_tokens, src.total_calls, src.cost, CASE WHEN src.cost > 0 THEN 'PRICED' WHEN src.cost = 0 AND src.input_tokens + src.output_tokens + src.cache_read_tokens + src.cache_write_tokens = 0 THEN 'NO_CHARGE' ELSE 'UNPRICED' END, -- Deliberate and uniform; see this changeSet's comment for why the true purse is not -- recoverable and why INSTANCE is the side to err on. 'INSTANCE', src.occurred_at FROM ( SELECT j.id, j.workspace_id, j.job_type, j.llm_model, COALESCE(j.llm_total_input_tokens, 0) AS input_tokens, COALESCE(j.llm_total_output_tokens, 0) AS output_tokens, COALESCE(j.llm_cache_read_tokens, 0) AS cache_read_tokens, COALESCE(j.llm_cache_write_tokens, 0) AS cache_write_tokens, GREATEST(COALESCE(j.llm_total_calls, 1), 1) AS total_calls, -- Guarded cast: llm_cost_usd is DOUBLE PRECISION, so historical bad data (a -- divide-by-zero upstream producing NaN/Infinity, or an absurd magnitude) would -- abort the whole migration mid-CAST. Store NULL — unverifiable, which surfaces as -- such — rather than throw or invent a number. The $1M-per-job ceiling is a -- plausibility bound, not the column's capacity (cost_usd holds far more): no single -- agent job legitimately costs that, so a value at or above it is corrupt, and -- letting it through would blow past every budget cap as if it were real spend. It -- is checked against the value ROUNDED to the stored 6-decimal scale, not the raw -- double, so that 999999.9999999 — which rounds UP past the bound — is judged on the -- number actually stored. CASE WHEN j.llm_cost_usd IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN j.llm_cost_usd = 'NaN'::double precision THEN NULL WHEN j.llm_cost_usd = 'Infinity'::double precision THEN NULL WHEN j.llm_cost_usd = '-Infinity'::double precision THEN NULL WHEN ABS(ROUND(j.llm_cost_usd::numeric, 6)) >= 1000000 THEN NULL ELSE ROUND(j.llm_cost_usd::numeric, 6) END AS cost, COALESCE(j.completed_at, j.created_at) AS occurred_at FROM agent_job j WHERE (COALESCE(j.llm_total_calls, 0) > 0 OR j.llm_cost_usd IS NOT NULL) AND NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM llm_usage_event e WHERE e.source_type = 'AGENT_JOB' AND e.source_id = j.id AND e.source_attempt = 0) ) src;

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.onFailMessage: llm_usage_event missing — nothing to backfill into

changeSet.comment:
Backfill the ledger from mentor turn history in chat_message.metadata. Tolerates both the nested {usage:{input,...}} shape and legacy flat inputTokens keys; float token counts floor to bigint (mirroring the reader). Every value is regex- and length-guarded before it is cast: metadata is free-form JSONB written by historical app versions, so one malformed row (a non-numeric string, "NaN"/"Infinity", or a value wider than the target column) would abort the ENTIRE migration on a raw cast. Anything that fails the guard becomes NULL, which the token COALESCEs treat as "no value" and the cost column treats as UNPRICED — never a silent $0. After this, code never aggregates over the JSON again; the ledger is the accounting source.
funding_source is INSTANCE for the same reason, and on the same evidence, as changeSet -10.
changeSet.sql: -- As in changeSet -10: every value is extracted once in the inner SELECT, and the outer one -- both stores and classifies from those, so the recorded cost and its pricing_state can -- never disagree. INSERT INTO llm_usage_event (id, workspace_id, job_type, source_type, source_id, source_attempt, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, total_calls, cost_usd, pricing_state, funding_source, occurred_at) SELECT gen_random_uuid(), src.workspace_id, 'MENTOR_TURN', 'MENTOR_TURN', src.id, 0, src.model, src.input_tokens, src.output_tokens, src.cache_read_tokens, src.cache_write_tokens, 1, src.cost, CASE WHEN src.cost > 0 THEN 'PRICED' WHEN src.cost = 0 AND src.input_tokens + src.output_tokens + src.cache_read_tokens + src.cache_write_tokens = 0 THEN 'NO_CHARGE' ELSE 'UNPRICED' END, -- Uniform INSTANCE, as in changeSet -10. 'INSTANCE', src.occurred_at FROM ( SELECT m.id, t.workspace_id, NULLIF(COALESCE(m.metadata->>'model', ''), '') AS model, COALESCE( floor(CASE WHEN length(m.metadata->'usage'->>'input') < 50 AND m.metadata->'usage'->>'input' ~ '^[0-9]{1,15}(\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN (m.metadata->'usage'->>'input')::numeric END), floor(CASE WHEN length(m.metadata->>'inputTokens') < 50 AND m.metadata->>'inputTokens' ~ '^[0-9]{1,15}(\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN (m.metadata->>'inputTokens')::numeric END), 0 )::bigint AS input_tokens, COALESCE( floor(CASE WHEN length(m.metadata->'usage'->>'output') < 50 AND m.metadata->'usage'->>'output' ~ '^[0-9]{1,15}(\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN (m.metadata->'usage'->>'output')::numeric END), floor(CASE WHEN length(m.metadata->>'outputTokens') < 50 AND m.metadata->>'outputTokens' ~ '^[0-9]{1,15}(\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN (m.metadata->>'outputTokens')::numeric END), 0 )::bigint AS output_tokens, COALESCE( floor(CASE WHEN length(m.metadata->'usage'->>'cacheRead') < 50 AND m.metadata->'usage'->>'cacheRead' ~ '^[0-9]{1,15}(\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN (m.metadata->'usage'->>'cacheRead')::numeric END), floor(CASE WHEN length(m.metadata->>'cacheReadTokens') < 50 AND m.metadata->>'cacheReadTokens' ~ '^[0-9]{1,15}(\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN (m.metadata->>'cacheReadTokens')::numeric END), 0 )::bigint AS cache_read_tokens, COALESCE( floor(CASE WHEN length(m.metadata->'usage'->>'cacheWrite') < 50 AND m.metadata->'usage'->>'cacheWrite' ~ '^[0-9]{1,15}(\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN (m.metadata->'usage'->>'cacheWrite')::numeric END), floor(CASE WHEN length(m.metadata->>'cacheWriteTokens') < 50 AND m.metadata->>'cacheWriteTokens' ~ '^[0-9]{1,15}(\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN (m.metadata->>'cacheWriteTokens')::numeric END), 0 )::bigint AS cache_write_tokens, -- Same plausibility bound as changeSet -10, applied to the ROUNDED value: the -- regex's integer-digit guard only bounds the unrounded string, and -- "999999.9999999" passes it but rounds to seven integer digits. CASE WHEN length(m.metadata->>'costUsd') < 50 AND m.metadata->>'costUsd' ~ '^-?[0-9]{1,6}(\.[0-9]+)?$' AND ABS(ROUND((m.metadata->>'costUsd')::numeric, 6)) < 1000000 THEN ROUND((m.metadata->>'costUsd')::numeric, 6) END AS cost, m.created_at AS occurred_at FROM chat_message m JOIN chat_thread t ON t.id = m.thread_id WHERE m.metadata IS NOT NULL AND (m.metadata->>'costUsd' IS NOT NULL OR m.metadata->'usage'->>'input' IS NOT NULL OR m.metadata->>'inputTokens' IS NOT NULL) AND NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM llm_usage_event e WHERE e.source_type = 'MENTOR_TURN' AND e.source_id = m.id AND e.source_attempt = 0) ) src;

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Instance-owned LLM provider connection: endpoint, credential and wire protocol. app_admin-owned, global.

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Instance-curated model behind a connection: opaque upstream id, capability, lifecycle and visibility. (connection_id, upstream_model_id) is unique because the usage recorder matches a call's frozen binding by that pair alone and just takes the first enabled match — two entries for the same pair would make pricing nondeterministic and let a free sibling silently shadow a priced one.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE llm_model ADD CONSTRAINT ck_llm_model_visibility CHECK (visibility IN ('PUBLIC','GRANTED'));

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Effective-dated price rows for an instance model, with a tri-state pricing_mode. The surrogate PK fixes the retired model_pricing table's fatal model-id-as-PK (which made a second price row a PK collision). Repricing closes the open row's effective_to and inserts a new one in one transaction; the partial unique index is the backstop against a double-open race. Rates are per 1M tokens (what every vendor quotes) at NUMERIC(18,8), so sub-cent-per-1M rates do not truncate to zero.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE llm_model_price ADD CONSTRAINT ck_llm_model_price_mode CHECK (pricing_mode IN ('PRICED','NO_CHARGE','UNPRICED')); ALTER TABLE llm_model_price ADD CONSTRAINT ck_llm_model_price_shape CHECK ( (pricing_mode = 'PRICED' AND per_1m_input_usd IS NOT NULL AND per_1m_input_usd >= 0 AND per_1m_output_usd IS NOT NULL AND per_1m_output_usd >= 0 AND (per_1m_cache_read_usd IS NULL OR per_1m_cache_read_usd >= 0) AND (per_1m_cache_write_usd IS NULL OR per_1m_cache_write_usd >= 0) AND GREATEST(per_1m_input_usd, per_1m_output_usd, COALESCE(per_1m_cache_read_usd, 0), COALESCE(per_1m_cache_write_usd, 0)) > 0) OR (pricing_mode = 'NO_CHARGE' AND note IS NOT NULL AND btrim(note) <> '' AND per_1m_input_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_output_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_cache_read_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_cache_write_usd IS NULL) OR (pricing_mode = 'UNPRICED' AND per_1m_input_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_output_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_cache_read_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_cache_write_usd IS NULL) ); ALTER TABLE llm_model_price ADD CONSTRAINT ck_llm_model_price_window CHECK (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to > effective_from); CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_llm_model_price_open ON llm_model_price (model_id) WHERE effective_to IS NULL;

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Which workspaces may use a GRANTED-visibility instance model. Composite PK, modelled on account_feature: an allowlist by reference, so revoking needs no data migration. sfk_ = scalar FK (ADR 0017) — a pure join table with no JPA @ManyToOne, so Hibernate emits the columns but never these constraints; the prefix keeps them out of the drift diff while preserving referential integrity in the database.

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Workspace-owned LLM connection: same shape as the instance one, but tenant-scoped — the workspace admin owns the key and the bill. (id, workspace_id) is unique so a model row can carry a same-workspace FK: without it a model could claim workspace A while pointing at workspace B's connection, and thus decrypt B's key.

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Workspace-owned model with its current price inline (a single workspace's own rate needs no audit history). workspace_id is denormalised rather than implied through connection_id so every query carries a workspace_id predicate for the tenancy inspector, and the (connection_id, workspace_id) FK guarantees a model can never bind another tenant's connection — and so never decrypt its key.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE workspace_llm_model ADD CONSTRAINT ck_ws_llm_model_pricing_mode CHECK (pricing_mode IN ('PRICED','NO_CHARGE','UNPRICED')); ALTER TABLE workspace_llm_model ADD CONSTRAINT ck_ws_llm_model_price_shape CHECK ( (pricing_mode = 'PRICED' AND per_1m_input_usd IS NOT NULL AND per_1m_input_usd >= 0 AND per_1m_output_usd IS NOT NULL AND per_1m_output_usd >= 0 AND (per_1m_cache_read_usd IS NULL OR per_1m_cache_read_usd >= 0) AND (per_1m_cache_write_usd IS NULL OR per_1m_cache_write_usd >= 0) AND GREATEST(per_1m_input_usd, per_1m_output_usd, COALESCE(per_1m_cache_read_usd, 0), COALESCE(per_1m_cache_write_usd, 0)) > 0) OR (pricing_mode = 'NO_CHARGE' AND price_note IS NOT NULL AND btrim(price_note) <> '' AND per_1m_input_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_output_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_cache_read_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_cache_write_usd IS NULL) OR (pricing_mode = 'UNPRICED' AND per_1m_input_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_output_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_cache_read_usd IS NULL AND per_1m_cache_write_usd IS NULL) );

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Instance LLM settings singleton (id pinned to 1): the egress allowlist governing EVERY connection, and the workspace-connection enable flag. An empty allowlist means allow all, so an upgrade is non-breaking. There is deliberately no unpriced-usage policy knob: enforcement is structural — a capped workspace whose month is unverifiable is always blocked (a cap you cannot verify is not a cap) and an uncapped one never is.

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.onFailMessage: ck_auth_event_event_type already admits the LLM catalog event types
preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'ck_auth_event_event_type' AND pg_get_constraintdef(oid) LIKE '%LLM_SETTINGS_CHANGED%'

changeSet.comment: Admit the instance LLM catalog's audit events on auth_event. The catalog is global, and config_audit_event.workspace_id is NOT NULL, so these changes cannot live there; auth_event is the same ledger the account admin already uses for APP_ROLE_CHANGED. The ADD validates every existing row in one pass under a momentary ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, no rewrite.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE auth_event DROP CONSTRAINT ck_auth_event_event_type; ALTER TABLE auth_event ADD CONSTRAINT ck_auth_event_event_type CHECK (event_type IN ( 'LOGIN', 'LOGIN_FAILED', 'LOGOUT', 'TOKEN_REFRESH', 'JWT_REVOKED', 'IDENTITY_LINKED', 'IDENTITY_UNLINKED', 'IMPERSONATION_BEGIN', 'IMPERSONATION_END', 'ACCOUNT_DELETED', 'EXPORT_REQUESTED', 'APP_ROLE_CHANGED', 'RESEARCH_CONSENT_REVOKED', 'LLM_CONNECTION_CREATED', 'LLM_CONNECTION_UPDATED', 'LLM_CONNECTION_DELETED', 'LLM_MODEL_CREATED', 'LLM_MODEL_UPDATED', 'LLM_MODEL_DELETED', 'LLM_MODEL_PRICE_CHANGED', 'LLM_MODEL_SHARING_CHANGED', 'LLM_SETTINGS_CHANGED' ));

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: When a QUEUED job becomes eligible for a poll-loop claim; backoff-computed on requeue.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE agent_job ADD COLUMN available_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(); ALTER TABLE agent_job ALTER COLUMN available_at DROP DEFAULT;

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_index i JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid WHERE c.relname = 'ix_agent_job_queued_available' AND i.indisvalid

changeSet.comment:
Index queued jobs by their claim-eligibility time without blocking queue traffic.
The guard is on pg_index.indisvalid, not on the index merely existing: a CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY that fails partway leaves an index the planner will never use, and JDBC index metadata cannot tell it apart from a good one. An existence-only precondition would record this changeSet as applied and leave the queue's poll query unindexed for the life of the install. The leading DROP clears exactly that leftover and is a no-op otherwise.

rollback.sql: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS ix_agent_job_queued_available;

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'ck_agent_job_status'

changeSet.comment: CHECK the six documented job statuses at the storage layer; NOT VALID keeps the lock momentary, changeSet -29 validates.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE agent_job ADD CONSTRAINT ck_agent_job_status CHECK (status IN ('QUEUED','RUNNING','COMPLETED','FAILED','TIMED_OUT','CANCELLED')) NOT VALID;

rollback.sql: ALTER TABLE agent_job DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS ck_agent_job_status;

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Bounded attempt counter for the delivery-recovery sweep, so a poisoned delivery cannot retry forever.

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment:
Oban's autovacuum recommendation, adapted: a high-churn queue table needs vacuum triggered by absolute row-change count, not the default 20% scale factor.
The precondition checks only that the table is there, and deliberately does not try to detect the storage parameters themselves. A precondition can see WHETHER a reloption is set but not whether it holds the intended value, so matching on presence would let a stale or half-applied setting silently skip the change. ALTER TABLE ... SET (...) is idempotent, so this reasserts the intended values outright. Consequence, stated rather than hidden: a re-run overwrites operator-tuned values for these two parameters on this table. Tune them by changing this changelog, not the live table.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE agent_job SET (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0, autovacuum_vacuum_threshold = 500);

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Same autovacuum tuning for worker_registry — a small table taking heartbeat-rate UPDATEs. Reasserted unconditionally on re-run for the reason given in changeSet -24.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE worker_registry SET (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0, autovacuum_vacuum_threshold = 100);

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_index i JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid WHERE c.relname = 'ix_agent_job_delivery_pending' AND i.indisvalid

changeSet.comment: Support the zombie sweeper's stuck-PENDING-delivery scan. Guarded on index validity, not existence — see changeSet -21.

rollback.sql: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS ix_agent_job_delivery_pending;

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_index i JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid WHERE c.relname = 'ix_agent_job_retention' AND i.indisvalid

changeSet.comment: Support the retention service's terminal-row batch scans (strip, then delete). Guarded on index validity, not existence — see changeSet -21.

rollback.sql: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS ix_agent_job_retention;

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'sfk_feedback_agent_job' AND confdeltype = 'c'

changeSet.comment: Harden feedback.agent_job_id from CASCADE to RESTRICT. CASCADE transitively took feedback_observation, feedback_placement and reaction with it — append-only research and product data. The retention service's delete pass already excludes jobs referenced by feedback, but leaving the FK on CASCADE means any FUTURE agent_job delete (a bug, an ad-hoc admin query, a retention path added later) could silently repeat it.

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'ck_agent_job_status' AND NOT convalidated

changeSet.comment: Validate ck_agent_job_status under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE (reads and writes unblocked).
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE agent_job VALIDATE CONSTRAINT ck_agent_job_status;

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Distinguish claimed preparation from provider-capable execution, so a crashed job is billed for the calls it actually made.
changeSet.sql: UPDATE agent_job SET execution_started_at = started_at WHERE status = 'RUNNING' AND started_at IS NOT NULL

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Retire the legacy per-1k model_pricing table. It has no runtime consumer: mentor and practice cost both derive from the admission-frozen per-1M price snapshot, and the usage ledger freezes the applied rates per event as the authoritative price history.

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Exactly one model per (workspace, purpose). Replaces the named agent_config profile and the scalar practice/mentor config pointers on workspace. A binding points at either an instance model or a workspace-owned one, never both and never neither.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE workspace_agent_binding ADD CONSTRAINT ck_workspace_agent_binding_single_model CHECK (num_nonnulls(instance_model_id, workspace_model_id) = 1);

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.onFailMessage: the workspace LLM catalog is already populated — legacy configs were migrated or the catalog was configured by hand

changeSet.comment:
Carry every workspace's existing AI configuration into the new catalog BEFORE agent_config is dropped (changeSet -39).
agent_config is the only place an instance holds a workspace's LLM endpoint, model name and API key. The key is encrypted with the same converter the new tables use, so the ciphertext copies verbatim and the operator does not have to re-enter a secret they may no longer have. Dropping the table without this step destroys all of it irrecoverably.
WHAT IS CARRIED: every config that was doing something — one a workspace explicitly pointed at, OR one that is simply enabled. A NULL practice_config_id / mentor_config_id never meant "unused"; it meant "use the fallback", and both features had one. The mentor fell back to the workspace's oldest enabled config, and practice detection fanned out to ALL enabled configs. The documented default provisioning route (AGENT_DEFAULT_CONFIG_*) seeded exactly that shape: an enabled config with both pointers NULL, serving both features. Carrying only pointed-at rows would silently destroy the live key of every instance provisioned that way.
Only a config that is BOTH disabled AND unreferenced is dropped: nothing could reach it, and neither resolver would ever have selected it. changeSet -34 names those workspaces in the deploy log before the table goes.
WHAT IS BUILT: one connection per carried config, one model per connection, and one binding per (workspace, purpose) carrying that config's timeout, concurrency and internet limits verbatim. A config serving both purposes yields one connection and two bindings.
The bindings reproduce what each resolver actually selected, not what the pointer column said: • MENTOR — the pointed-at config when it exists and is enabled, else the workspace's oldest enabled config, else no binding (the mentor could not run at all in that state). • PRACTICE_DETECTION — the pointed-at config when the pointer is set, enabled or not (a bound-but-disabled config PAUSED detection, and a disabled binding is that same pause), else the oldest enabled config. A dangling or cross-tenant pointer yields no binding, which is also what it did before. (workspace, purpose) is unique, so a workspace that ran detection across SEVERAL enabled configs collapses to one binding — the oldest. Nothing is lost: the other configs still arrive as connections and models, ready to bind. changeSet -34 names those workspaces.
EVERYTHING LANDS DISABLED, including configs that look complete. In PROXY credential mode — the default, and what the startup seeder wrote — the sandbox never used the config's own base URL: it called the in-app proxy, which forwarded to an INSTANCE-level upstream URL set by environment variable. That value is not in the database, so no migration can know which endpoint was really in force. Enabling automatically could silently re-point a workspace's traffic, and its API key, at a different host. Carrying everything forward disabled loses nothing and guesses nothing; an admin reviews the pre-filled endpoint and switches it on.
Endpoint fallbacks, in order: the config's own base URL, then the provider's documented public endpoint for OpenAI and Anthropic, then an explicitly unresolvable placeholder for a provider whose endpoint was never recorded anywhere (Azure OpenAI, whose resource host only ever lived in configuration). The placeholder uses the reserved .invalid TLD so it can never resolve, and the row it sits on is disabled. changeSet -34 reports these.
A config that never named a model gets the same treatment: upstream_model_id is NOT NULL, so it takes the placeholder 'model-not-migrated' rather than being skipped. Skipping would drop the binding — and with it that workspace's timeout, concurrency and internet limits, which exist nowhere else once the table is gone — and would leave the operator no trace of which purposes the workspace had wired. Such a config could not run before either (the seeder warns about it), so the placeholder costs nothing and, being disabled, cannot call anything. changeSet -34 reports these too.
api_protocol is openai-completions for every carried-over row: it is the protocol the legacy runtime used for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and it is one of only two the new schema admits. An Anthropic endpoint does not speak it — such a row is carried forward for its key alone and is reported by changeSet -34 as needing a real endpoint.
Slugs are legacy-<config id>: deterministic, inside the 64-character limit, and unique without collision handling because config ids are unique and both catalog tables are created empty in this same file (the precondition above enforces that).

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.onFailMessage: MIGRATION NOTICE (#1368): at least one workspace AI configuration needs a human before it will run again — a provider that is not OpenAI-compatible, no endpoint URL ever recorded, no model name ever recorded, detection that ran across several configurations at once (only one binding survives), or a configuration that was both disabled and unreferenced and is therefore dropped with the old table. Every other carried-over value — endpoint, model, API key, limits — was preserved. Everything arrives disabled; open each workspace's AI settings, fix what the server log names, and re-enable. See MIGRATION.md. (Re-applying this changelog against an already-upgraded database — after Liquibase's tracking table has been cleared or rebuilt — also prints this notice, because the legacy table it inspects is gone by then; expected, and safe to ignore. An ordinary re-run skips this changeSet entirely, and a fresh install never prints it: the legacy table is created empty by an earlier changelog and has nothing to report.)

and.sqlCheck: SELECT ( (SELECT count(*) FROM agent_config c WHERE (c.enabled OR EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM workspace w WHERE w.id = c.workspace_id AND (w.practice_config_id = c.id OR w.mentor_config_id = c.id))) AND (c.llm_provider <> 'OPENAI' OR NULLIF(btrim(c.llm_base_url), '') IS NULL OR NULLIF(btrim(c.model_name), '') IS NULL)) + (SELECT count(*) FROM agent_config c WHERE NOT c.enabled AND NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM workspace w WHERE w.id = c.workspace_id AND (w.practice_config_id = c.id OR w.mentor_config_id = c.id))) + (SELECT count(*) FROM workspace w WHERE w.practice_config_id IS NULL AND (SELECT count(*) FROM agent_config c WHERE c.workspace_id = w.id AND c.enabled) > 1) )

changeSet.comment:
Report, at deploy time, everything about the carry-over an operator has to act on rather than just re-enable. The precondition fails (WARN, and this changeSet then still runs) when any of the three cases below applies; the body writes server-log warnings naming the affected workspaces, because the precondition message is static and by the time an operator reads it agent_config is gone. The predicate mirrors changeSet -33's carry-over rule exactly — anything -33 could not reproduce faithfully must be named here, or it is lost in silence.
The body re-checks that the table is there rather than trusting the precondition: onFail WARN executes the changeSet regardless of why the precondition failed, and "the legacy table no longer exists" is one of those reasons.

changeSet.author: hephaestus

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Daily ECB euro reference rates, for DISPLAY ONLY: USD remains the sole unit of record, pricing and enforcement, and nothing here is ever read by a budget gate, an admission decision or the usage ledger. usd_per_eur is stored in the ECB's own direction — dollars per ONE euro — so the historical record is exactly what was published; the inversion happens once, at read time. Global: an exchange rate is a property of the world, not of a tenant. The unique rate_date is also the arbiter when two replicas fetch at once — the loser's insert fails and is swallowed, rather than duplicating the day.

changeSet.comment: Drop agent_job.llm_cost_usd — the ledger is the single accounting source, and this column was DOUBLE PRECISION (money in a binary float). Its values were already copied into llm_usage_event.cost_usd as NUMERIC(18,6) by changeSets -10/-11 above, so this must stay after them. Nothing reads it: the JPA mapping and the DTO field are gone.

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Per-call usage accumulators for a mentor turn, mirroring agent_job's. The proxy meters each call as it is served so the budget gate can see a turn's own spend before the turn ends; these columns make that survive a worker crash, which an in-memory meter cannot. The in-flight reaper bills from them instead of booking a crashed turn as zero tokens.

changeSet.comment: Drop three agent_job columns nothing reads. llm_api_key is never written — the proxy resolves the credential live from the catalog, so a stale copy here would only ever be a second place for a key to leak from. network_id and container_id are never written either; container_id was projected into the API, where it read as permanently null.

changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'ex_llm_model_price_no_overlap'

changeSet.comment:
No two price windows for the same model may overlap. This is the guard -14 could not express: ck_llm_model_price_window constrains a single row, ux_llm_model_price_open constrains only the open row, and neither can see a PAIR of closed windows. Inside an overlap a usage event prices two different ways depending on which row the lookup happens to pick — on a money table that is a silent, unreconcilable divergence, not a display bug.
btree_gist supplies the `=` operator class GiST needs for the model_id equality half of the constraint. It is stock contrib, bundled in every official Postgres image and in docker/postgres/Dockerfile, and the very first changeSet of this schema (1780825201546-1-extensions) already runs an unconditional CREATE EXTENSION for citext — so this asks for no privilege the installer did not already need, and a role that cannot create an extension cannot install Hephaestus at all. llm_model_price is created above in this same changelog, so no existing instance holds rows the ADD could fail to validate.
Immediate (not DEFERRABLE) is correct for the one writer: LlmModelService#updatePrice closes the open row at `now` and flushes BEFORE inserting the new row at effective_from = `now`, and tstzrange is half-open, so [.., now) and [now, ..) do not overlap at any point in the transaction. That flush ordering is already load-bearing for ux_llm_model_price_open and is commented as such at the call site.

rollback.sql: ALTER TABLE llm_model_price DROP CONSTRAINT ex_llm_model_price_no_overlap;

preConditions.onFailMessage: ck_auth_event_event_type already admits the login-provider event types
preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'ck_auth_event_event_type' AND pg_get_constraintdef(oid) LIKE '%LOGIN_PROVIDER_DELETED%'

changeSet.comment: Admit login-provider administration on auth_event. Creating, editing or deleting a login provider changes how every person authenticates to this instance — the single event an audit trail exists for — and it shipped unaudited because config_audit_event.workspace_id is NOT NULL and these changes belong to no workspace. auth_event is where they belong on the merits, not as a fallback: it is already the ledger for APP_ROLE_CHANGED, the impersonation pair and the instance LLM catalog, and it is the trail an instance admin reads at /admin/audit. The ADD validates every existing row in one pass under a momentary ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, no rewrite.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE auth_event DROP CONSTRAINT ck_auth_event_event_type; ALTER TABLE auth_event ADD CONSTRAINT ck_auth_event_event_type CHECK (event_type IN ( 'LOGIN', 'LOGIN_FAILED', 'LOGOUT', 'TOKEN_REFRESH', 'JWT_REVOKED', 'IDENTITY_LINKED', 'IDENTITY_UNLINKED', 'IMPERSONATION_BEGIN', 'IMPERSONATION_END', 'ACCOUNT_DELETED', 'EXPORT_REQUESTED', 'APP_ROLE_CHANGED', 'RESEARCH_CONSENT_REVOKED', 'LLM_CONNECTION_CREATED', 'LLM_CONNECTION_UPDATED', 'LLM_CONNECTION_DELETED', 'LLM_MODEL_CREATED', 'LLM_MODEL_UPDATED', 'LLM_MODEL_DELETED', 'LLM_MODEL_PRICE_CHANGED', 'LLM_MODEL_SHARING_CHANGED', 'LLM_SETTINGS_CHANGED', 'LOGIN_PROVIDER_CREATED', 'LOGIN_PROVIDER_UPDATED', 'LOGIN_PROVIDER_DELETED' ));
